title: Reciprocating Compressor

introduction.definition: A reciprocating compressor raises gas pressure with a piston moving back and forth in a cylinder. Automatic suction and discharge valves let gas in and out. In a double-acting cylinder both ends compress gas alternately; the crankshaft, connecting rod and crosshead convert the motor's rotation into straight-line piston motion.
applications: Process gas compression in refineries and petrochemical plants
key_points: Positive displacement — flow nearly independent of pressure
Best for high pressure ratios and small-to-medium flows
Valves are the most frequent maintenance item
introduction.summary: A reciprocating compressor squeezes gas with a piston moving in a cylinder. In this double-acting, crosshead-type machine both ends of the cylinder work: while one end draws gas in through its suction valves, the other end compresses gas and pushes it out through its discharge valves. Automatic plate valves open and close only by the pressure difference across them.

what_to_look_for: The motor turns the crankshaft; the connecting rod drives the crosshead back and forth.
The piston rod transmits this motion through the packing to the piston.
As the piston moves away from one end, pressure there falls and the suction valve opens — gas flows in.

steps.text: The motor turns the crankshaft; the connecting rod drives the crosshead back and forth.
The piston rod transmits this motion through the packing to the piston.
As the piston moves away from one end, pressure there falls and the suction valve opens — gas flows in.
On the return stroke the trapped gas is compressed; when it exceeds discharge pressure the discharge valve opens.
The other end of the cylinder works the opposite way at the same time (double-acting).
Pulsation bottles smooth the intermittent flow before the piping.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Capacity ≈ swept volume × volumetric efficiency; volumetric efficiency falls as the pressure ratio rises (clearance-volume re-expansion).

components.key_components: Cylinder, piston & rings, plate valves, crosshead, crankshaft, distance piece, pulsation bottles

foundation: Use a massive concrete block foundation or skid designed for the unbalanced forces and couples; grout the frame.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Follow the pulsation/acoustic study (API 618): bottle sizes, orifice plates, pipe support spacing.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

routine.task: Check frame oil level and pressure, cylinder lubrication rate, cooling water.
Monitor valve cover temperatures (a hot valve is leaking).

periodic.task: Check rod run-out and rider band wear (rod drop).

overhaul.task: Replace piston rings, rider bands and packing; check liner wear.
Inspect crankshaft, bearings and crosshead clearances.

lubrication: Frame (crankcase) oil by splash or pressure lubrication; cylinders and packing by a separate lubricator (lubricated machines).

A reciprocating compressor raises gas pressure with a piston moving back and forth in a cylinder.
Automatic suction and discharge valves let gas in and out.
In a double-acting cylinder both ends compress gas alternately; the crankshaft, connecting rod and crosshead convert the motor's rotation into straight-line piston motion.

script.narration: How the Reciprocating Compressor works.
The motor turns the crankshaft; the connecting rod drives the crosshead back and forth.
The piston rod transmits this motion through the packing to the piston.
As the piston moves away from one end, pressure there falls and the suction valve opens — gas flows in.
On the return stroke the trapped gas is compressed; when it exceeds discharge pressure the discharge valve opens.
The other end of the cylinder works the opposite way at the same time (double-acting).
Pulsation bottles smooth the intermittent flow before the piping.

video_tutorials.title: Reciprocating Compressor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Reciprocating Compressor.
Check frame oil level and pressure, cylinder lubrication rate, cooling water.
Monitor valve cover temperatures (a hot valve is leaking).
Inspect and recondition valves.
Check rod run-out and rider band wear (rod drop).
Replace piston rings, rider bands and packing; check liner wear.
Inspect crankshaft, bearings and crosshead clearances.
Watch for valve failure: high discharge temperature. Common cause: broken plates/springs.
Watch for packing leakage: gas at the distance-piece vent. Common cause: worn rings.
Watch for high vibration / pulsation: pipe shaking. Common cause: acoustic resonance.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why does a double-acting compressor deliver about twice the flow of a single-acting one of the same size?
options: Both ends of the cylinder compress gas
questions.explanation: Each stroke compresses gas on one side.

questions.question: What opens the suction and discharge valves?
What is the purpose of the crosshead?
options: To take the side thrust so the piston rod moves in a straight line
questions.explanation: Rod packing then seals a purely axial motion.
